To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a novel targeted adenosine-associated virus/phage (AAV/phi) suicide vector is effective for cancer therapy, that it has an additional mechanism of killing cancer cells, and that it has a bystander effect between endothelial and cancer cells.
a heterotypic bystandander effect between endothelial and cancer cells is involved in the cytotoxic mechanism of targeted suicide gene therapy for cancer.

the targeted suicide gene transfer to tumor vascular endothelum results in the death not only of the tumor endothelial cells, but also of tumor cells through the induction of a heterotypic bystandander effect.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of novel gene therapy approaches to cancer, in particular the targeted delivery of genes to tumor blood vessels, which can be used to treat cancer patients.
the development of a novel gene therapy approach for cancer treatment.
the development of novel therapeutic strategies for the treatment of cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the bystander effect is a complex phenomenon, and it is not yet clear whether it occurs in the tumor microenvironment.

the heterotypic bystandder effect between endothelial and nonendothelial cancer cells is mediated by gap junctions and that this effect is responsible for tumor growth suppression in vivo after systemic gene therapy with targeted suicide genes such as HSVtk.

the heterotypic bystandander effect between endothelial and cancer cells is an important mechanism of action of the targeted AAV/phage suicide gene therapy approach, which is not only mediated by gap junctions but is also independent of the primary gene transfer into tumor vascular endothelum in vivo.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that the tumor endothelium can be targeted by a targeted gene delivery system.
the tumor endothelium is a promising target for gene therapy, and the bystander effect is a novel and potentially synergistic mechanism of tumor cell killing.
the targeted delivery of suicide genes into nonmalignant cells of the tumor microenvironment (e.g., endothelial cells) can lead to tumor cell death through a novel heterotypic bystandder effect.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have developed a new gene delivery platform for the targeted delivery of suicide genes into tumor endothelial cells.
the endothelial cells are not the only cells that are responsible for killing tumor cells.
endothelial and tumor stromal cells can be killed by a heterotypic bystandander effect, which may have important implications for cancer gene therapy.
